# v1.1.0-dev.76 — Dialogs open six times faster

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.75`.

## They Were Slow, And Now They Are Not

Making every dialog its own window last release cost something nobody
asked to pay: opening one went from instant to a beat of nothing.

Measured, rather than guessed at: **160ms**, of which **7ms** was
creating the window. All the rest was loading the app's page into it.

So one dialog window is now kept alive and hidden with the page already
loaded, waiting to be told which dialog to become. Opening one is a
`show()` call. Measured after: **22–29ms**, across the settings dialog,
the window editor and the display editor.

That rests on one fact, which was checked before it was relied on: a
modal window disables the app when it is *shown*, not when it is
created — so a spare one can sit there without freezing anything. The
app re-checks that at runtime every time it prepares a spare, and turns
the whole optimisation off for the session if it ever turns out to be
wrong.

## Release Notes You Can Actually Read

The notes box in the update dialog was a fixed 280px letterbox with the
rest of the dialog empty below it. It now fills whatever the window
gives it, and follows the window when you resize it.

## Dialogs Read As Windows

The border around both the app window and every dialog is a single
consistent colour, and the shadow is the real thing — the one the
operating system draws around a window — rather than a shading trick
painted inside the frame, which only ever looked like a vignette.

## Every Dialog Knows What Size It Can Wear

A dialog is a window you can drag by the corner, so "this breaks below
500px wide" needs to be a limit the window enforces rather than
something you find out by doing it. Each one now declares the size its
own layout actually needs: the settings dialog won't go below the width
of its tab rail plus a panel, a two-column form keeps room for two
columns.

Dialogs that are a fixed amount of content have a ceiling too. Stretching
a yes/no confirm across a 4K display isn't bigger, it's one sentence
adrift in a field of background.

## Assign Hotkey Is A Panel Again

It went back to being an immovable panel over the app rather than its
own window. Its entire job is to swallow the next key combination you
press, and a separate window that owns focus in its own right is the
wrong shape for that.

## Two Bugs Worth Naming

The update dialog would have opened **empty**. It reads the pending
update out of the app window's memory, and a dialog window has its own —
so it found nothing and rendered a blank box. The update now travels
with the request, and the "is there anything to show" check happens
before a window is created rather than after.

The safety check on the spare window asked "is the app disabled?" to
detect whether preparing a spare had broken something. When a spare was
prepared *while a dialog was open*, the app was disabled — correctly, by
that dialog. The check read that as its own doing, switched the
optimisation off for the rest of the session, and re-enabled the app
window out from under an open modal. It only asks that question when no
dialog is open now.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
